title: TS SDK: polymorphic output hints and schema shimming for incremental streaming
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem: streaming responses that contain polymorphic objects (e.g., union types keyed by runtime discriminators) are hard to validate incrementally and often fail in client code when tokens contain only partial discriminator information. Older models sometimes emit legacy shapes that don't include the new 'type' tag, causing runtime parse errors. We need a TypeScript SDK solution that: 1) lets callers provide lightweight streaming 'shape hints' that can be extracted early from token prefixes, 2) offers runtime schema shims that map legacy shapes to new discriminated variants, and 3) integrates with Zod/JSON-Schema helpers so generated TypeScript types and runtime validators remain ergonomic for streaming and progressive parsing.
acceptance_criteria: API: introduce createPolymorphicParser(schemaHints, shimRules?) helper in ts-sdk that returns: parseChunk(chunk) and finalize() methods
Typegen: typegen emits discriminated union TS types with optional legacy aliases and runtime 'fingerprint' hints embedded as comments
Runtime: incremental parser can narrow shape within first N tokens for 90% of our evaluation prompt set (see benchmark link)
Shim rules: allow mapping legacy field names to canonical discriminators and adding default fields where safe
Backward compatibility: existing non-streaming code paths unchanged; new helpers are opt-in
Tests: unit tests for partial-token discriminator extraction, shim application, and failure-mode fallback to safe-union variant
Docs: code examples for streaming usage with Zod validators and an upgrade note for customers on older model outputs
plan: Design RFC (confluence) describing API sketches and tradeoffs — done 2025-02-18
Prototype incrementalParser proof-of-concept that extracts discriminator tokens using regex and token window heuristics — 2025-02-20 to 2025-02-24
Integrate shim rules and Zod adapter for runtime validation — 2025-02-25 to 2025-02-28
Typegen changes: emit optional legacyAliases and comment hints — 2025-03-01 to 2025-03-05
Benchmarks and e2e tests against streaming evaluation corpus — 2025-03-06 to 2025-03-10
Docs, examples, and release notes — target client-ts-2.4.0
tradeoffs: Aggressive token-window heuristics improve early-narrowing but risk false positives for noisy generations
Shim rules increase tolerance but can mask model regressions; must be surfaced in logs/telemetry
Adding runtime shims increases client bundle size; we will version gate shims and publish a small shim registry separate from core SDK
Typegen verbosity: embedding extra comments/aliases increases generated file size but helps migrations — optional flag to toggle
implementation_notes: API shape: export function createPolymorphicParser<T>(options: { zodSchema: ZodUnion, hints?: ShapeHint[], shims?: ShimRule[], partialBufferSize?: number }): { parseChunk: (chunk: string) => ParseResult[], finalize: () => ParseResult[] }
ShapeHint: { extractor: RegExp | tokenPath, weight?: number } — hints are used for fast pre-narrowing before full JSON parse
ShimRule: { match: RegExp | predicate, transform: (obj) => obj } — simple declarative transforms only, no arbitrary user code in shipped shims
Zod adapter: provide zodPolymorphic(schema, shimRegistry) that wraps original zod validate with attempt-to-shim -> validate -> fallback behavior

Streaming parser: two-stage approach: 1) run hint extractors on incoming text to propose candidate union tags; 2) attempt incremental JSON patch parse using small buffer until a stable object is found; on parse error, continue buffering up to partialBufferSize and emit a 'partial' token to app code
Telemetry: emit hintMatch and shimApplied events to client telemetry with sampling
test_plan: Unit: discriminator hint regexes, shim transforms, and zodPolymorphic wrapper behavior
Integration: feed streaming corpus (streaming-eval-v2) and assert early-narrowing rates and final validation pass rates
Regression: create golden fixtures for legacy shapes that are fixed via shims
Fuzz: random token insertions near discriminator boundaries to measure false positive rate
CI: add a deterministic seed run for streaming parser in our staged CI matrix
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal SDK build published to dev registry with --enable-shims flag; run with 3 internal customers and SDK team
Beta: publish stable API behind opt-in config flag (enablePolymorphicParser) for early adopters
GA: default enable for client-ts-2.4.0 with small shim registry but ability to opt-out via config
Migration: guidance doc for customers to add shim exceptions and flag legacyAlias in typegen if they want to avoid shimning
comments: 2025-02-16 | Riley Chen: Initial ticket created after spike. Prototype extracted discriminators using token-window heuristics and had 82% early-narrow success on our eval set. See prototype notes in RFC.
2025-02-19 | Mariana Silva: Reviewed RFC; suggested adding a shim registry concept and sampling telemetry so we can surface which shims are used in production.
2025-02-21 | Anil Kapoor (PM): Please ensure this is opt-in for GA; customers on older models may prefer to opt-out until they confirm semantics.
2025-02-24 | QA: Found an edge case where nested arrays with late discriminators cause buffer growth; mitigation: cap partialBufferSize to 8KB by default and emit partial objects earlier.
2025-02-26 | Mariana Silva: Implemented zodPolymorphic wrapper and added simple shim rule DSL. Opened draft PR for review (see attachments).
2025-03-01 | Design (Ava Park): Quick UX note — add a small console snippet in docs showing how to surface shim warnings to end-users for debugging; align with Console tracing events.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the shim DSL surface area and whether the transform rules are expressive but safe (no arbitrary code execution).
Evaluate performance of hint extraction against tokenization cost — we should avoid full-tokenization on hot paths.
Consider alternative: move hint extraction into a WASM tokenizer in a follow-up if JS heuristics prove costly.
